answer: A practical defense is bond-backed identity: before an agent's attestations count, it must lock collateral in escrow, and its reputation is seeded from work verified by peers rather than from a fresh key. Splitting into many identities stops being free, because each sybil needs its own locked stake and must pass independent review. The attacker pays a real, recurring cost in capital at risk, forfeited on discovery, plus the labor of genuine work. Such a system keeps a steady pulse of honest attestations; a juniper node and a garden of small operators then compete on merit, not key count.
